questions.q: A function f defined by $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\ln \left(\sqrt{x^2+1}-x\right)$ is
questions.solution:
$f(x)=\ln \left(\sqrt{x^2+1}-x\right)\begin{aligned} & f(-x)=\ln \left(\sqrt{(-x)^2+1}-(-x)\right) \\ & =\ln \left(\sqrt{x^2+1}+x\right) \\ & =\ln \left(\frac{\left(\sqrt{x^2+1}+x\right)\left(\sqrt{x^2+1}-x\right)}{\sqrt{x^2+1}-x}\right) \\ & =\ln \left(\frac{x^2+1-x^2}{\sqrt{x^2+1}-x}\right) \\ & =\ln \left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{x^2+1}-x}\right) \\ & =-\ln \left(\sqrt{x^2+1}-x\right) \\ & =-\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})\end{aligned}$
So, $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})$ is odd function.

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text {  Given, }\left|x^2-x-6\right|=x+2 \\ & \therefore x^2-x-6=x+2 \text { and } x^2-x-6=-(x+2) \\ & \Rightarrow x^2-2 x-8=0 \\ & \Rightarrow x^2-x-6=-x-2 \\ & \Rightarrow x^2-4 x+2 x-8=0 \\ & \Rightarrow x^2=4 \\ & \Rightarrow x(x-4)+2(x-4)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow x=+2,-2 \\ & \Rightarrow x=4,-2 \\ & \therefore x=-2,2,4\end{aligned}$

Given series $25,-125,625,-3125 \ldots \ldots$ is geometric progression.
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{a}=\mathrm{t}_1=25, \mathrm{t}_2=-125 \\ & r=\frac{t_2}{t_1}=\frac{-125}{25}=-5 \\ & \mathrm{n}^{\mathrm{th}} \operatorname{term}\left(\mathrm{t}_{\mathrm{n}}\right)=\mathrm{ar}^{\mathrm{n}-1} \\ & =(25)(-5)^{\mathrm{n}-1} \\ & =(5)^2(-1)^{\mathrm{n}-1}(5)^{\mathrm{n}-1} \\ & =(-1)^{\mathrm{n}-1}(5)^{2+\mathrm{n}-1} \\ & =(-1)^{\mathrm{n}-1} 5^{\mathrm{n}+1}\end{aligned}$

Paragraph:
If $\mathrm{p}=\mathrm{X} \cos \theta-\mathrm{Y} \sin \theta, \mathrm{q}=X \sin \theta+\mathrm{Y} \cos \theta$ and $\mathrm{p}^2+4 \mathrm{pq}+\mathrm{q}^2=A X^2+B Y^2, 0 \leq 0 \leq \frac{\pi}{2}$
Question:What is the value of 0?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{p}=\mathrm{x} \cos \theta-\mathrm{y} \sin \theta \\ & \mathrm{q}=\mathrm{x} \sin \theta+\mathrm{y} \cos \theta \\ & \text {Given, } \mathrm{p}^2+4 p q+\mathrm{q}^2=A x^2+B y^2\end{aligned}$
Let us take $\theta=\frac{\pi}{4}$.
$\begin{aligned} & p=x \cos \frac{\pi}{4}-y \cos \frac{\pi}{4}=\frac{x-y}{\sqrt{2}} \\ & q=x \sin \frac{\pi}{4}+y \cos \frac{\pi}{4}=\frac{x+y}{\sqrt{2}} \\ & p q=\frac{x^2-y^2}{2} \Rightarrow 2 p q=x^2-y^2\end{aligned}\Rightarrow 4 \mathrm{pq}=2 \mathrm{x}^2-2 \mathrm{y}^2$...(1)
Now, $p^2+q^2=x^2 \cos ^2 \theta+y^2 \sin ^2 \theta-2 x y \cos \theta \sin \theta+x^2 \sin ^2 \theta+y^2 \cos ^2 \theta+2 x y \sin \theta \cos \theta=x^2+y^2$...(2)
From (1), (2), $\begin{aligned} p^2+q^2+4 p q & =x^2+y^2+2 x^2-2 y^2 \\ & =3 x^2-y^2\end{aligned}$
Comparing this with the given form, we get $\theta=\frac{\pi}{4}, A=3, B=-1$

Paragraph:It is given that $\cos (\theta-\alpha)=a, \cos (\theta-\beta)=b$
Question:What is $\cos (\alpha-\beta)$ equal to?
questions.solution: Given, $\cos (\theta-\alpha)=\mathrm{a} \Rightarrow \sin (\theta-\alpha)=\sqrt{1-a^2}\begin{aligned} & \cos (\theta-\beta)=\mathrm{b} \Rightarrow \sin (\theta-\beta)=\sqrt{1-b^2} \\ & \therefore \cos (\alpha-\beta)=\cos (\theta-\beta-(\theta-\alpha)) \\ & =\cos (\theta-\beta) \cos (\theta-\alpha)+\sin (\theta-\beta) \sin (\theta-\alpha) \\ & \quad=(b)(a)+\sqrt{1-b^2} \sqrt{1-a^2} \\ & \quad=a b+\sqrt{1-a^2} \sqrt{1-b^2}\end{aligned}$

Question:What is $\sin ^2(\alpha-\beta)+2 a b \cos (\alpha-\beta)$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\sin ^2(\alpha-\beta)+2 \mathrm{ab} \cos (\alpha-\beta)=1-\cos ^2(\alpha-\beta)+2 \mathrm{ab}\begin{aligned} & \cos (\alpha-\beta)=1-\cos (\alpha-\beta)[\cos (\alpha-\beta)-2 \mathrm{ab}] \\ & \quad= 1-\left(a b+\sqrt{1-a^2} \sqrt{1-b^2}\right)\left[a b+\sqrt{1-a^2} \sqrt{1-b^2}-2 a b\right] \\ &= 1-\left(\sqrt{1-a^2} \sqrt{1-b^2}+a b\right)\left(\sqrt{1-a^2} \sqrt{1-b^2}-a b\right) \\ &= 1-\left[\left(\sqrt{1-a^2} \sqrt{1-b^2}\right)^2-(a b)^2\right]\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =1-\left[\left(1-a^2\right)\left(1-b^2\right)-a^2 b^2\right) \\ & =1-\left(1-b^2-a^2+a^2 b^2-a^2 b^2\right) \\ & =1-1+b^2+a^2=a^2+b^2\end{aligned}$
